newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Trust to acquire pension businesses.
newsitem.headline: Royal Trust to acquire pension businesses.

text.p: Royal Trust, a unit of Royal Bank of Canada, said on Thursday it has agreed to acquire the institutional, pension custody and related businesses of Montreal Trust, a unit of Bank of Nova Scotia.
Under the terms of the agreement, Royal Bank will acquire approximately C$120 billion in client assets under administration, the bank said in a statement.
The price of the transaction was not disclosed.

"This is a major strategic step for the Royal Bank Financial Group as it moves us up to one of the top ten custodians worldwide, enabling us to more effectively compete internationally," said David Dunlop, senior vice-president of global securities services at Royal Trust.

Last August, Royal Bank acquired the institutional custodial assets of Toronto-Dominion Bank and its subsidiary, TD Trust. Scotiabank said it concluded that the resources required to become a major player in the custody business would be better applied to areas such as stock transfer and corporate trust.
The deal is expected to close on March 31, subject to due diligence and regulatory approvals.
